Ray-marched scalar volumes

Source: R/layers-volume.R
geom_volume_3d.Rd

Renders a complete rectilinear grid per raster sample. Coordinates are interpreted in transformed scale units. Samples are trilinearly interpolated. Absorption uses front-to-back emission-absorption integration in linear light and stops at the nearest opaque mesh or traced surface. Translucent raster geometry inside the volume composites at its depth: the integral is split at each fragment. Overlapping volumes combine their extinction and emission at each sample. Vector and hybrid panels place the volume as an image; a vector primitive is drawn under it where it lies behind the depth at which the image reaches half its opacity.

Usage

geom_volume_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  mode = c("absorption", "mip", "iso"),
  opacity = c(0, 1),
  colours = c("#132B43", "#56B1F7"),
  samples = 256L,
  level = NULL,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, ..., show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments. Map x, y, z and value to the grid coordinates and scalar field.

mode

"absorption", "mip" or "iso".

opacity

Nonnegative extinction coefficients per transformed data unit, as an evenly spaced numeric ramp over the scalar range, or a function of scalar values. A constant coefficient s over distance d transmits exp(-s*d).

colours

Colour ramp, or a function mapping scalar values to colours.

samples

Number of integration steps across the volume diagonal. Grid-cell boundaries also split integration intervals.

level

Isovalue for mode = "iso"; defaults to the scalar-range midpoint.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

MIP finds the maximum of the interpolated field along each ray. Isosurfaces find the first root of the cubic field along each crossed grid cell, including roots between equal-sign cell endpoints, and use its analytic gradient. These modes are independent of the absorption sampling count.

References

Max (1995). Optical models for direct volume rendering. IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 1, 99-108. doi:10.1109/2945.468400

Examples

a <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8)
d <- expand.grid(x = a, y = a, z = a)
d$v <- with(d, exp(-4 * (x^2 + y^2 + z^2)))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, value = v)) +
  geom_volume_3d(opacity = c(0, 3), samples = 32) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster", dpi = 60))
